newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM sticks to 2.6 pct of GDP deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM sticks to 2.6 pct of GDP deficit goal.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday the cabinet, which began debating the 1997 budget, was likely to stick to the finance ministry's deficit target of 2.6 percent of gross domestic product.

Cimoszewicz said a slightly higher deficit was conceivable. But room for maneouvre was limited by the government's ability to finance the deficit and its ambition to slash inflation to 13 percent from this year's target of 17-18 percent.

"We are likely to keep this deficit (of 2.6 percent of GDP). Even though I personally feel that if it were a 0.1 point higher, it would not make a substantial difference," Cimoszewicz said before the cabinet meeting.
"But we have to take into account first, our ability to finance the deficit and secondly, the effect of the deficit on inflation because we'd like to meet our targets," he added.
The government agreed in July to cut the deficit from this year's 2.8-percent target during its debate on the general budget outline.

But only last week, it received the detailed finance ministry draft of the bill. Some analysts speculated the final budget bill proposal might assume a bigger shortfall to make room for higher spending in the election year.
The government has to submit its final draft to parliament by the end of this month and then, parliament will have three months to pass the bill.
